feature_notes: Streaming replies parse through a separate 48-slot ring so each flush does not evict finished messages from the 800-entry block cache; a slot is matched when the earlier text is a prefix-extension of the new one
extends() compares only the first 64 bytes and the 64 bytes ending at the earlier length when the earlier text is longer than 128 bytes; shorter texts use a full utf8 starts(with:)
MarkdownView.== makes finished replies skip re-rendering entirely; MarkdownBlockView.== returns true for two settled blocks in the same slot without comparing content

Delegation code fences are recognised by info string exactly "hydra", "hydra-sent" or "hydra-leaving" (lowercased); they render as HydraDelegationBlock(json:sent: info != "hydra") instead of a code block

"hydra-leaving" renders at opacity 0, scaleEffect 0.98 anchored .top, and allowsHitTesting(false) while still occupying its space; its transition is .asymmetric(insertion: .softAppear, removal: .identity), every other block uses .softAppear

Paragraph rendering branches: links -> InlineText(hasLinks: true); not streaming and listDepth == 0 and a head name is mentioned -> InlineText(hasLinks: true) (AppKit path for hover); listDepth == 0 with mention segments -> VeiledText(segments:); otherwise InlineText(hasLinks: false)
Mention matching is word-bounded (neither neighbour is a letter or number) and tries longest names first, so 'Hank 2' wins over 'Hank'

warm() parses up to 24 texts per call, taking candidates from the first 96 texts, skipping any text over 262144 utf8 bytes and stopping once 1048576 bytes have been queued; it also pre-builds RichLink runs off the main thread

Bare URLs display as a pretty title: forge reference first (!<id> for GitLab merge_requests, #<id> for issues and GitHub pull/issues), then a cached video title capped at 48 chars with a trailing ellipsis, else host plus last path segment

prettyTitle drops 'www.' prefixes, returns the host alone when the last segment is one of watch, view, index, index.html, index.php, home, default, page; a segment over 24 chars is cut to 21 plus an ellipsis; a title over 40 chars becomes prefix(19) + ellipsis + suffix(18)
compactFallback applies the same 19/18 split to hostless URLs longer than 40 characters
Every link run is forced bold by inserting .stronglyEmphasized into its existing inline presentation intent

isBareDisplay strips whitespace, a surrounding <...>, and trailing characters from ".,;:!?)]}>"; then treats a display equal to the absolute string, or any http(s) prefixed string without spaces or newlines, as bare

Bare domains typed in chat are autolinked to https://<match> only when the last label is in the curated bareDomainTLDs set (comprehensive list of gTLDs and ccTLDs, 'com'..'pe'); runs already carrying a link or the .code intent are left alone
Autolinking trims trailing punctuation from the set ".,;:!?'\"" off a match before building the URL

Favicons are never requested for non-public hosts: empty, "localhost", any host containing ':' (IPv6), any of .local .localhost .localdomain .internal .intranet .lan .home .home.arpa .test .invalid .corp, any single-label host, and IPv4 in 0.x, 10.x, 127.x, 169.254.x, 192.168.x, 172.16-31.x, 100.64-127.x

Fetched icons are scaled so the longest side is at most 64px, flood-filled from the border to strip a white plate (alpha > 200, min channel >= 236, channel spread <= 20), edge pixels with a plate neighbour and min channel >= 160 are un-premultiplied to alpha = 1 - min/255 (dropped entirely below alpha 0.02), and finally rasterised at 28x28 into a 14x14 point NSImage
Code blocks over 120 lines render only their first 120 lines with a toggle; the line count is a newline byte count, not a split, deliberately to keep hover cheap
Tables over 30 rows render the first 30 with a 'Show all N rows' button; there is no way back to collapsed (the button only toggles showsAll, and the button is hidden once showsAll is true)

ProseReflow unwraps hard-wrapped prose before copying: needs 2+ lines, no open fence language, no leading whitespace, no line starting with #>-*+| or a digit followed by '.' or ')', every line but the last at least 45 characters, no line but the last ending in {};:=([\| or '->' or '=>', no double spaces or tabs anywhere, and the joined text must contain a sentence break matching the regex "[.!?] "
CopyButton shows a checkmark for 1.4 seconds after copying, then reverts via a task holding only the binding
markdownBlockSelection defaults to true, so every rendered block is individually selectable; whole-reply copying goes through MessageText

MarkdownView.warm's 'stable' handling: streamingParse returns MarkdownParser.Parse.stable, but the exact rule the parser uses to decide a block is final is in MarkdownParser, not this file.

The environment flag markdownProseRuns defaults to true but nothing in this file sets it to false; which call site (if any) disables the ProseRunView path could not be determined from the assigned files.
AnyTransition.softAppear, Chrome.accent, Font.chat(...) and RecentCache are used but defined elsewhere, so their exact durations/colors/eviction policy are not established here.

feature_notes: This path is the non-streaming alternative to MarkdownView's per-block stack, chosen when markdownProseRuns is true and isStreaming is false; it merges a whole prose run into one selectable AppKit text view
Code, table and rule blocks are explicitly skipped by both collect() and append(), because MarkdownView.segments never puts them in a prose run
joinedSources concatenates paragraph/heading/list-item/quote text with "\n" and is used both as the link-fetch source and as the coordinator's change key

The re-render check fires when any of source, pointSize, dimmed, revision, mention names, or the head-name-to-URL map changes; onOpenHead and mergeTarget are assigned outside that check so a fresh environment closure always lands
makeNSView sets passesProseThrough = false, so this view (unlike the single-paragraph LinkParagraphView) handles its own prose events rather than passing them through
dismantleNSView nils delegate, onOpenHead and mergeTarget to break retain cycles when the row scrolls away

The hover handler and the fetch task capture only the weak box, the bindings, a name-to-persona dictionary and the targets map, never the view value, so a scrolled-away run does not keep its styled text alive
The head-mention popover only shows when the hovered name's target URL matches the URL baked into the text AND a persona with that name exists; it re-shows only when the hovered threadID changes
The link-asset task is keyed by RichLink.linkAssetKey (hosts + video ids), so streamed or re-laid-out text with no new link does no work; streaming is always passed as false on this path

files.purpose: Flattens a whole markdown message into plain text for the clipboard, by walking the app's own parsed MarkdownBlock tree rather than the raw source: headings and paragraphs as their inline text, code verbatim, links rewritten to 'title (url)', the hydra delegation block dropped. Backs the row menu's Copy message action.

Replacements are applied in reverse match order so earlier ranges stay valid while the string is mutated in place
Quote blocks lose their marker entirely: their children are appended at the same level with no '>' prefix
List item children are appended via the same append(), so nested blocks land as flat lines with no extra indentation
A block-level regex failure (NSRegularExpression init throwing) silently returns the text untouched
The file name is a leftover: the doc comment states the selectable text view it used to hold left with the whole-reply drag mode and this enum is all that stayed

Dissolve curve: alpha = 1 - pow(1 - progress, 1.6)
Backlog boost: boost = 1 + 0.3 * max(0, chunkCount - 2), so 3+ chunks in flight speed each other by 30% per extra chunk

feature_notes: Documented as a port of zeron's crates/ui/src/markdown/veil.rs, itself a port of mugen-markdown's FadePainter; layout is committed at once and only paint animates, so nothing moves or resizes
The first advance() adopts the current text as the baseline and fades nothing, so a row scrolled back into view or a thread switched back to mid-reply does not re-fade what is already on screen

A rewrite that is not a pure append keeps the common prefix's chunks and re-veils only the changed tail; chunks whose start is past the new common prefix are dropped whole, explicitly to avoid constructing an inverted Range (which would trap)
advance() is idempotent for unchanged text, so a SwiftUI body may call it on every evaluation
spans() only returns chunks with alpha < 1 worth painting; consumers additionally filter where span.alpha < 1
Both clocks skip their frame entirely while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling, holding the last painted frame and resuming when the scroll ends
VeilClock tears its display link down the moment now >= deadline; run(until:) extends an existing deadline with max()

settledText() calls veil.reset() when the reply is no longer veiled, so a finished paragraph holds no copy of its own text; while still streaming the baseline is kept so a quiet beat does not make the next flush arrive unveiled

VeiledText(segments:) joins only the .prose segments into the veiled AttributedString and records each prose run's end index in the JOINED string's own character clustering, precisely because a grapheme spanning a join counts as one character of the join but two across the runs
VeiledText(verbatim:) keeps code as a plain String and only builds an AttributedString on frames that actually veil, so a finished code dump costs nothing on hover
fadingText() reads VeilClock.shared.now purely to subscribe to the tick, but paints at Date.now so the first frame after a flush is never stale
LinkTextVeil tracks the widest painted NSRange and clears it before every repaint and on settle, intersecting with the current storage length so a shrunken text cannot over-remove

LinkTextVeil.update(_:active:) with active == false lets chunks in flight finish and then forgets the text (settle keepText: false); detach(_:) stops the clock and clears when the view leaves its window
Span ranges are clamped to 0..<count on both consumers before slicing, so a chunk that outlives a shrink cannot index past the end
